steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: (It's been a long time since I last felt hot blood flowing in my veins.)

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: (Not since I left the battlefield and left my homeland have I...)
His vision begins to blur from the loss of blood. Everything seems covered in a white glow, and he instinctively closes his eyes.
He hears the song of a harp, but he does not know from whence it comes.
He forces his eyes open, and sees himself in an unfamiliar space. He seems to be floating in mid-air, people passing in front of his eyes without acknowledging him.
It is as though he is in a dream.

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: I will never work with the Sargonians! Beat me, torture me, kill me if you want—

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: But you won't get one word out of me about the guerrillas!

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: So there are guerrillas.

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: ...Skata!

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: Why are you so angry? I thought Minoans liked logic. That's what the stories of heroes all say.

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: Are you trying to butter me up? I'm not talking!

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: No need to be so on edge. Just wanted to have a conversation. I don't like interrogating people either.

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: But I'll be reprimanded if I don't spend enough time in here. Nothing I can do.

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: What are you doing, Mashayer? Are you so stupid you can't do something as simple as interrogate a prisoner?

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: I'm on it, sir!

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: Piece of trash. Some noble. Pah.
The prisoner watches as his interrogator jumps up from the ground nervously, while his superior leaves after casually hurling a few words of abuse.
Both seem used to such a situation. It is as though the officer cusses and abuses the guard on a daily basis.
The guard's complexion is young and pale. He is thin and mild-mannered, very different from the villagers' impression of Sargonians.
The prisoner warns himself not to let his guard down.
Sargonians are cunning. Perhaps the two of them conspired to put on an act.

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: Well, I have to act like I'm interrogating you.

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: Could you... say something? Anything.

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: Anything? I've got a litany of curses for you. I could go on for days.

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: ...Let's talk about something else. Something nicer, something that can help us forget about our struggles and helplessness... tell me some Minoan heroic stories.

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: I know some of your legends from ancient books that I collected, but they're not easy to find in Sargon.

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: You already told this story a couple of days ago. I remember.

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: Tsk.

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: Anything else? Think!

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: (Weren't we just putting on a show for his superior? Why is he taking such careful notes?)

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: (Why would a Sargonian love Minoan legends so much? Is there something not right with this guy's head?)

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: You've only told a hundred or so. There must be more stories and legends in the land of heroes.

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: (Trying to provoke me? Not falling for that!)

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: Fragments you heard from the elders as a child are fine. It doesn't need to be complete or popular.

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: The kind of story that would make a little Sargonian girl dream about Minos... there must be more, right?

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: (Skata... well, if that's what he wants...)

spans.text: ... well, if that's what he wants...)

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: (I'll just make one up. It's not like this idiotis Sargonian could tell.)

spans.text: (I'll just make one up. It's not like this

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: Alright. Let me tell you about Siopi, the silent hero.
It is the strangest experience the prisoner has ever had. No one would believe the story if he told it. He decided to take it with him to his grave—
If he ever gets out of here.

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: Bloody bother. Finally got him off my back for the day.

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: I didn't know I was so good at making up stories. I should become a bard if I ever get out.

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: If I ever get out...

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: Is that a crack in the door?

steps.name: Minoan Captive
steps.text: Did that ilithios forget to lock the door?
It has been a long time since he last saw the stars. It almost feels like he is dreaming as he breathes the air of freedom again.
Is he out? Is he free? Just like this?

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: Useless trash! You've been in that Minoan's cell every single day, and you haven't gotten one scrap of intel about the guerrillas?

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: S-Sorry, sir. I've been taking records, but he contradicts himself every day. I... I'm afraid nothing he says can be trusted.

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: I knew you couldn't get anything done! Incompetent fool!

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: I'll interrogate him tomorrow while you watch and learn how things are done in the lord ameer's army!

steps.name: Sargonian Guard
steps.text: Y-Yes, sir...
The fugitive hears the guard and his superior talking in the distance. He hastens his movement through the bushes.
The movement seems to have drawn the attention of the Sargonians.

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: How did the prisoner get out?!

steps.name: Sargonian Officer
steps.text: After him, Mashayer, you worthless shit! You are DEAD, if you don't catch him!
Hearing the sound made by the skinny guard's ill-fitting armor sets the fugitive's heart at ease.
He knows a single Sargonian could never catch him, on this Minoan land.
He takes one final look back as he escapes the Sargonian camp.
The fugitive sees the frail guard stumble and fall. The guard's luxurious armor, probably an heirloom, weighs him down so much that he struggles to get himself off the ground.
Or perhaps... he just wanted an excuse to not get up?
Did he really forget to lock the door, or did he finally find an opportunity to leave a crack?
The prisoner does not know.
The only thing that the prisoner knows is that he will never forget the time he spent at the Sargonian camp, and the ridiculous-looking Sargonian.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: (What... is this?)

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: It's my father.
Xanthos turns around in surprise, and sees the Sargonian woman, standing in the same vision as he.
There is surprise on her face, yes, but also nostalgia and poignance.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I know he came to Minos in the lord ameer's army, but was sent back to Sargon for his incompetence. He would have received a heavier punishment, but what little glory the House of Mashayer had left protected him one last time.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: He never really... achieved anything, and it wasn't a surprise that he would mess up after he was conscripted. He didn't like to talk about his time in Minos, and I never asked...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I didn't know this was where those stories of the Minoan heroes he told me came from.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: He's very different from my image of a Sargonian.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Yes. He was always weak and soft, never talking back even when insulted to his face... I always wondered why he loved heroic stories so much, when he was the furthest thing from a hero.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: No wonder... no wonder he told me the story of Siopi the silent hero so many times, the hero who kept a secret for thirty years...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: He planted the seed of heroes in your heart.

steps.name: Padishah Khery
steps.text: I have high hopes for you, Medjehtiqedti Nasutu Mashayer.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: It is an honor.

steps.name: Padishah Khery
steps.text: Do you understand why I appointed someone like you to lead the mission, someone so young and inexperienced?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: You must have your reasons.

steps.name: Padishah Khery
steps.text: You're much smarter than your father was.

steps.name: Padishah Khery
steps.text: The House of Mashayer was a noble house with a rich tradition, and I was on good terms with your elders.

steps.name: Padishah Khery
steps.text: It pained me to see the family fall on hard times under your father, who was frail and idle.

steps.name: Padishah Khery
steps.text: I arranged a cushy post for him in the lord ameer's army in Minos, safely away from the frontlines, and he almost got himself into a court-martial.

steps.name: Padishah Khery
steps.text: When Minos came up again after all these years, you were the first person I thought of.

steps.name: Padishah Khery
steps.text: Young Medjehtiqedti is much sharper than her father, I thought. I'm sure she will have no trouble bringing a harp to Minos and bringing back a few blueprints that belonged to Sargon to begin with.

steps.name: Padishah Khery
steps.text: You'll do a fine job and do your family proud, won't you?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Yes, exalted padishah! I loved the legends of Minos, and I've wanted to see true heroism with my own eyes since I was little. I'll make sure the Minoan mission goes perfectly!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The padishah said a bunch of flowery words to me before I left, but I never understood why he made me the head of this mission.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I guess it's because it's easy to get rid of me, if something goes wrong.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: And I had no idea that those 'blueprints' contained such detailed records.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Frankly, I don't really care about doing the Mashayer name proud.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I came because I wanted to see this land that I've always been fascinated by with my own eyes, to chase the legends that I've only heard about...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Or perhaps, I wanted to find some answers about my father...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: What is this land of heroes that father talked about really like, and what is the heroic spirit really like? I wanted to learn, to find out. That's why I came to Minos.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Have you found the answer?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Yes. What about you?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I was once like you, Xanthos.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Pallas?! You too...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I've seen with my own eyes how our people died shielding their comrades from the Sargonians, and heard the screaming of the wounded being amputated in village huts.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Hate flowed in your heart and mine, in the hearts of every Minoan.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Even now... in my heart...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: But have you ever stopped to think why we love to drink?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Besides the sweet fragrance of wine and the joy of harvest that it represents, the inspiration and joy that it brings us...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Besides all that...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: It's also because it makes us forget, if only for a while.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Too many things trouble us and make us hurt, but we can't forget them completely, because to do so would be a betrayal, so we drown ourselves in drink, seeking a moment's forgetfulness.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: But then... I had to leave Minos.

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: You're Pallas, aren't you? The medics told me you often drink here.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Yes, I am... what is it?

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: You're Minoan, right? You've been in the Lachedamon competitions? Do you know Dikaiopolis, the Blood Knight? Did you ever fight him?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: No... but I've heard of him. A Minoan Infected who participates in the Kazimierz Majors, I think?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Well, actually, the 'competitions' in those two places are not quite the same thing...

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: But they're both clashes of physical ability and skill, aren't they?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Mm... well... uh...

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: I knew it! The principles of strength are the same everywhere! The Blood Knight must be strong because of his Minoan upbringing!

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: I wanted to meet the Blood Knight, but he's retired now.

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: Still, it's an honor to meet another Minoan master! Can I have your autograph? Anywhere's fine—how about my t-shirt?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: ...(Quietly signs)

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: Thank you so much!

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: So... do Minoans have a special way of training?

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: I heard you love drinking. Is this part of your training? Accelerating blood circulation with alcohol and increasing explosiveness?

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: The medics also say you can fall asleep anywhere! This must be a way to save energy! You only fully utilize your physical ability when necessary!

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: I see! This is why the Blood Knight was so explosive!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Er... these are just my personal habits. I don't know how the Blood Knight trains, but I doubt...

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: I get it, I get it, just fantasizing about things. Did I get carried away? I hope I didn't cause any offense.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: ...It's alright. You really love Dikaiopolis, don't you?

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: Yeah! I lost all hope after learning that I have Oripathy, but the Blood Knight gave me the will to live again.

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: I watched recordings of his bouts so many times! I've even started training myself, hoping to join an Infected Knightclub someday.

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: He was the one who blazed the trail for the Infected in Kazimierzian knightsports, paving the way for the Radiant Knight's return to the tournaments!

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: His bout with the Radiant Knight was one for the ages! I was there for it, and I cried when they took the podium together.

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: I wasn't sure why I cried. Maybe it's because I saw a flicker of hope for the future.

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: I guess he's the kind of hero the Minoans talk about!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: He's Infected. According to conventional Minoan wisdom...

steps.name: Knightsports Fan
steps.text: Do Infected heroes have some kind of special title in Minos?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: No... But he's a hero, yes. No one can deny it.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Traditions don't stay unchanged forever, Xanthos.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The stories of the heroes defined and shaped who we are. Yet, because heroes arise from among us, we in turn possess the power to define them and to reshape what it means to be a hero.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I learned that after I left Minos.

steps.name: Minoan Villager
steps.text: Our goddess of victory is back!

steps.name: Minoan Villager
steps.text: I heard you destroyed another Sargon cavalry unit that tried to sneak across the border?

steps.name: Minoan Girl
steps.text: I told you not to call me that when we're in the village... it's embarrassing.

steps.name: Minoan Girl
steps.text: It was the title that we gave to Pallas...

steps.name: Minoan Villager
steps.text: Whoever leads us to victory is our goddess of victory. That's what Pallas said when she left—

steps.name: Minoan Villager
steps.text: 'You can use this overblown title however you want, if it scares the Sargonians.'

steps.name: Minoan Villager
steps.text: As long as we still have our 'Goddess of Victory', you'll keep the Sargonians away.

steps.name: Minoan Girl
steps.text: Yeah... although Sargonian raiders still come every now and then, since she signed that 'Non-Aggression Pact' with Sargon's border tribes on behalf of the villages in the area...

steps.name: Minoan Girl
steps.text: The raids have been getting fewer and fewer after we won a few victories. It's all thanks to the reputation of the 'Goddess of Victory'.

steps.name: Minoan Girl
steps.text: Besides, inheriting Pallas's title makes me feel like I can't give up, which helps me pull through in tough battles.

steps.name: Minoan Girl
steps.text: It doesn't just scare our enemies; it also inspires our own.

steps.name: Minoan Villager
steps.text: Yeah, that's what heroes are for.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The village of Akroti... brings back so many memories.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It's very much like my homeland.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: All the villages of Minos are alike. The same soil nurtured us.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: But it's not just because of the same soil that we're a single nation. It's because we know the same stories.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Only we, upon seeing the olive branch, remember how the hero Pheidippides ran from Athenius to spread the news of our victory over the Sargonians to the other cities.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: He was carrying the olive branch of Athenius, and so it became the symbol of victory and hope to us.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: This is what truly belongs to us, something that outlanders and invaders cannot take away.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: As long as we keep living, we'll carry on these stories, and change the traditions so that the legends of Minos's heroes may continue, that the spirit of Minos may continue.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Minos is wherever we are.
It is a strange scene that unfolds before the eyes of the citizens of Athenius and the guests from Sargon and other city-states.
It is an exhilarating battle. But when the oar-wielding Minoan warrior's blood falls upon the strings of the harp in the hands of Kereseira's statue—
The ancient harp begins to make a sound, like an old machine starting up after a long slumber, its gears slowly beginning to turn.
As the harp begins to sing, the trio on the stage slows down, entering a trance-like state, sometimes angry, sometimes sad, sometimes laughing, sometimes weeping.
When the Minoan challenger is finally overcome by exhaustion and slumps down by the statue's pedestal, the other two on stage finally break out of their trance.
They look around themselves in confusion before running towards the challenger, reaching out to him to try to help him up, but getting no response from him.
The shouting, the cheering, and the angry yelling have all ceased. Those present begin to realize that they have witnessed a miracle.
The harp that stopped singing after the Sargonians invaded has returned to where it belonged, and declared—
The tradition continues, and a new chapter is written in the stories of the heroes.
The harp's music echoes in the sky above the square.
Xanthos looks up.
The autumn sun is painfully bright, but for some reason it seems to bring back dim memories, back to the day that he said goodbye to Ithakos.

a.text: Do you believe that the guerrillas can defeat the Sargonians?
Even though we've been losing for a century?

steps.name: Ferryman
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Ferryman
steps.text: I haven't received any divine revelations, and I can't tell the future. I can't even leave with you.

steps.name: Ferryman
steps.text: But I will promise what I can.

steps.name: Ferryman
steps.text: I'll protect our village, our houses, our farms and flowerbeds. Perhaps we can go to Athenius, where you came from, once you're victorious.

steps.name: Ferryman
steps.text: I'll still be a ferryman, ferrying you to your workplace at the temple on the other side of the city as the sun shines upon the Delphi Canal... I've been imagining the scene ever since you described it to me.

steps.name: Ferryman
steps.text: ...Are you listening, Ithakos?

a.text: Minos is in for a cold winter this year, brother.

steps.name: Ferryman
steps.text: Yes. But the spring will be all the warmer for it.
He finally remembers what he said to Ithakos.
And he remembers the warm smile on Ithakos's face at the answer.
The pain and anger of losing a dear friend had clouded his memory and caused him to forget what was most important.
But things will get better, when spring comes and war is over, when life gets back on track.
The wounds of the earth will heal, and the snowmelt from the peaks of Heria will continue to flow, bringing flowers and reeds home.
